metadata.purpose: Reference question-answer set for retrieval-augmented generation evaluation
notes: All ground-truth answers refer to the supplied research corpus and original attached papers.
Source_document_ids correspond to 01–10 text documents in the corpus ZIP.
Conflicting published numerical values are intentionally preserved with evaluation context.
Reported classifications are not clinical diagnoses.
Selected subset of original 30-question golden set; original_id retains provenance.

questions.question: What are the three main stages of the first stacked-ensemble study?
Which three feature types are extracted in the DU-POA study?
questions.ground_truth_answer: TF-IDF, improved Word2Vec, and style features.

questions.question: What are the four preprocessing steps in the IDCNN–SqueezeNet study?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Remove punctuation, URLs, and stop words; then tokenize the text.

questions.question: How does preprocessing in the stacked-ensemble study differ from the IDCNN–SqueezeNet study?
questions.ground_truth_answer: The stacked-ensemble study specifies stemming and stop-word removal, while IDCNN–SqueezeNet specifies punctuation removal, URL removal, stop-word removal, and tokenization.

questions.question: What role does SASSOA play, and which network does it optimize?
questions.ground_truth_answer: SASSOA is a weight-optimization method applied to the ICNN component of the Bi-GRU/Deep Maxout/ICNN ensemble; it is not an independent classifier.

questions.question: Why does the DU-POA study use modified mutual-information-based feature-level fusion?
questions.ground_truth_answer: To select or combine informative TF-IDF, improved Word2Vec, and style features, reducing the complication of keeping separate high-dimensional representations before classification.

questions.question: According to the IDCNN–SqueezeNet paper, what is its reported FNR and how does it compare with LSTM?
questions.ground_truth_answer: The hybrid FNR is 0.05 versus 0.17 for LSTM in the cited comparison.

questions.question: The DU-POA paper reports a dataset total of 4,288, yet 2,344 items in each class. Explain the discrepancy and what its train/test table implies.
questions.ground_truth_answer: The text is internally inconsistent: 2,344 + 2,344 = 4,688, not 4,288. Its listed train/test partitions (2,812/1,876; 3,281/1,407; 3,750/938; 4,219/469) also each total 4,688. The discrepancy cannot be resolved from the corpus alone and must be flagged, not silently corrected.

questions.question: Compare the feature-extraction approaches across all three studies without conflating feature methods with classifiers.
questions.ground_truth_answer: Study A uses n-grams, content, BoVW, LIWC, and improved semantic similarity; Study B uses TF-IDF, improved Word2Vec, and style features, followed by modified mutual-information-based fusion; Study C uses TF-IDF, n-grams, and BoW. These are input representations, not the Bi-GRU/ICNN, DBN/RNN/LSTM, or IDCNN/SqueezeNet classifier networks.

questions.question: Which ethical and scientific constraints would prevent turning the research classifiers directly into individual clinical diagnoses?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Social posts are incomplete and ambiguous evidence; labels may be keyword- or sentiment-based rather than clinically verified; model transfer across groups/platforms is uncertain; private posts can be sensitive; and both false alarms and missed signals carry risks. The studies present computational detection, not validated individual diagnoses.
